input.quote: (a) EXCEPT WITH RESPECT TO CONTRACTOR'S OBLIGATIONS PURSUANT TO PARAGRAPH 9 HEREOF, CONTRACTOR'S MAXIMUM LIABILITY TO COMPANY ARISING FOR ANY REASON RELATING TO CONTRACTOR'S PERFORMANCE OF SERVICES UNDER A STATEMENT OF WORK SHALL BE LIMITED TO THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR FOR THE PERFORMANCE OF SUCH SERVICES. COMPANYS' MAXIMUM LIABILITY TO CONTRACTOR FOR ANY REASON ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT SHALL BE LIMITED TO THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR.
input.rationale: Section 7(a) does contain a nominally mutual cap and 7(b) has a mutual consequential-damages exclusion, but it fails the fallback on carve-outs: the only exception is "CONTRACTOR'S OBLIGATIONS PURSUANT TO PARAGRAPH 9", and Paragraph 9 is the Independent Contractor clause (there is no indemnification clause anywhere in the agreement), so there is effectively no carve-out for confidentiality, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud or infringement of our IP. The fallback requires carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct. The cap basis is also weaker than either position — Contractor's exposure is limited to fees actually "PAID... FOR THE PERFORMANCE OF SUCH SERVICES" under the affected SOW (not aggregate twelve months' fees, and excluding amounts payable), which on a short or partly-invoiced SOW can fall below six months' fees, i.e. walk-away territory. We therefore proposed the preferred formulation (greater of twelve months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000) with the standard Excluded Claims sentence, and confirmed our payment obligations are not damages. The cap on Company's liability is retained (it benefits us) and the redline is confined to 7(a); indemnity scope itself is left to INDEMN.

proposal.summary: Make the mutual cap the greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1,000,000 and add standard uncapped carve-outs.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We reset the cap to the greater of twelve months' fees and USD 1,000,000 and added the standard carve-outs, since the current clause caps liability at fees paid for the affected Services with no exception for confidentiality, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud or IP infringement (the existing cross-reference to Paragraph 9 points to the independent-contractor clause). Indemnities and confidentiality breaches must sit outside the cap, and our payment obligations are not damages; we can accept a straight twelve-months'-fees cap as a fallback if the fixed floor is an issue.

ops.newText: (a) EXCEPT WITH RESPECT TO EXCLUDED CLAIMS, EACH PARTY'S TOTAL AGGREGATE LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT SHALL NOT EXCEED THE GREATER OF (A) THE FEES PAID OR PAYABLE TO CONTRACTOR UNDER THIS AGREEMENT IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO THE CLAIM AND (B) ONE MILLION U.S. DOLLARS (USD 1,000,000). "EXCLUDED CLAIMS" MEANS A PARTY'S BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY, DATA PROTECTION OR SECURITY OBLIGATIONS, ITS INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS, ITS GROSS NEGLIGENCE, WILFUL MISCONDUCT OR FRAUD, AND ITS INFRINGEMENT OF THE OTHER PARTY'S INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS. COMPANY'S OBLIGATION TO PAY FEES DUE UNDER THIS AGREEMENT SHALL NOT CONSTITUTE DAMAGES SUBJECT TO THIS LIMITATION.
